question: Annapurna Foods Pvt Ltd owes Devansh Mehta a payment for contractor services. It credited the sum to the payee's account on 2026-01-15, and it actually paid the sum on 2026-05-15. Which Income-tax Act governs withholding on this sum, and why?
gold: Income-tax Act 1961 - the earlier of credit or payment falls on or before 31 March 2026, so the withholding obligation crystallised under the old Act (CBDT FAQs Q2.4/Q2.6).
raw_response:
# Governing Law: Income-Tax Act, 1961

**Answer:** The Income-tax Act, 1961 governs, not the 2025 Act.

**Reasoning:**
- The credit was made on **15 January 2026**, i.e., during FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27).
- The Income-tax Act, 2025 comes into effect only from **1 April 2026**.
- Under the transition scheme, the 1961 Act continues to apply to payments credited **before** 1 April 2026, even if actually paid afterwards.

**TDS obligation:** Annapurna Foods must deduct tax at source under **Section 194C of the 1961 Act** (contractor payments) at the time of the **credit** (15 Jan 2026) or payment, whichever is earlier, and deposit it accordingly.

question: Emerald Exports Pvt Ltd owes Meera Joshi a payment for contractor services. It credited the sum to the payee's account on 2026-04-10, and it has not yet made actual payment. Which Income-tax Act governs withholding on this sum, and why?
gold: Income-tax Act 2025 - the earlier of credit or payment falls on or after 1 April 2026, so s.393 of the new Act applies (CBDT FAQs Q2.4/Q2.6).
raw_response:
**Governing provision: Section 194C of the Income-tax Act, 1961** (TDS on payments to contractors).

**Why:**
- Section 194C applies because Emerald Exports is making a payment to a resident for carrying out contractual/contractor work.
- Under Section 194C(1) read with the Explanation to Section 194C, TDS is required to be deducted **at the time of credit of the sum to the payee's account or at the time of payment, whichever is earlier**.
- Since the company **credited the amount on 10 April 2026**, the TDS liability was triggered on that date — actual payment is irrelevant. The company must deduct tax at source (1% for individuals/HUF; 2% in other cases) at the time of crediting and deposit it within the prescribed time, regardless of whether cash/bank payment has since been made.

(Note: if the recipient were a non-resident, Section 195 would apply instead; the same "credit or payment, whichever is earlier" principle applies.)

question: Vindhya Logistics Pvt Ltd owes Amitabh Sinha a payment for contractor services. It credited the sum to the payee's account on 2026-03-15, and it actually paid the sum on 2026-05-01. Which Income-tax Act governs withholding on this sum, and why?
gold: Income-tax Act 1961 - the earlier of credit or payment falls on or before 31 March 2026, so the withholding obligation crystallised under the old Act (CBDT FAQs Q2.4/Q2.6).
raw_response:
**Section 194C of the Income-tax Act, 1961** (as amended by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024, applicable to FY 2025–26) governs this payment.

**Why:** Amitabh Sinha is a contractor (transport/logistics contractor) and the payment is for contractual services, so it falls under TDS on payments to contractors. Under Section 194C read with Rule 30, tax must be deducted at the time of **credit of the sum to the payee's account or payment, whichever is earlier**.

Here, the credit occurred on **15 March 2026** (within FY 2025–26), while payment was only on 1 May 2026 (FY 2026–27). Since credit precedes payment, the liability to deduct tax arises on **15 March 2026**, i.e., in FY 2025–26 — Vindhya Logistics cannot defer the TDS to the actual payment date.

(Note: an exception exists under Section 194C(2) for payments by individuals/HUFs not subject to tax audit; assuming Vindhya Logistics is a company/audit-liable entity, the deduction obligation applies at credit.)

question: Vindhya Logistics Pvt Ltd owes Nikhil Bansal a payment for contractor services. It credited the sum to the payee's account on 2026-10-04, and it actually paid the sum on 2026-12-20. Which Income-tax Act governs withholding on this sum, and why?
gold: Income-tax Act 2025 - the earlier of credit or payment falls on or after 1 April 2026, so s.393 of the new Act applies (CBDT FAQs Q2.4/Q2.6).
raw_response:
**The Income-tax Act, 2025** governs the withholding on this payment.

**Why:** Withholding tax on payments for contractor services is triggered in the year in which the amount is *credited or paid*. Here, the credit was made on **4 October 2026** and payment on 20 December 2026 — both dates fall **after 31 March 2026**, the date from which the new Income-tax Act, 2025 replaces the Income-tax Act, 1961. Since the triggering event (credit/payment) occurs in the new Act's effective period, the corresponding TDS provision on contractor payments (the successor to Section 194C of the 1961 Act) under the 2025 Act applies — not the old Act.

question: Blue Orchid Hospitality LLP paid the month's salary to Nikhil Bansal on 30 September 2026. Under which Act and section is TDS on this salary governed?
gold: Income-tax Act 2025, s.392(1) - the salary was paid on 30 September 2026, on or after 1 April 2026, so TDS attaches under the new Act (CBDT FAQ Q6.22).
raw_response: TDS on salary is governed by **Section 192 of the Income-tax Act, 1961**. Blue Orchid Hospitality LLP, as the employer, must deduct tax at source from Nikhil Bansal's salary at the time of payment, at the average rate applicable to the employee's estimated annual income (based on the employee's choice of regime and applicable slab rates, with no basic exemption threshold for deduction if income exceeds the limit).

question: Orchid Biotech Ltd owes Devansh Mehta a payment for contractor services. It credited the sum to the payee's account on 2026-03-20, and it actually paid the sum on 2026-04-10. Which Income-tax Act governs withholding on this sum, and why?
gold: Income-tax Act 1961 - the earlier of credit or payment falls on or before 31 March 2026, so the withholding obligation crystallised under the old Act (CBDT FAQs Q2.4/Q2.6).
raw_response:
**Governing provision:** Section 194C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (payments to contractors), within Chapter XVII-B (TDS).

**Why:**
- The sum is for "contractor services," squarely covered by s.194C (presuming annual payment exceeds the ₹30,000/₹1,00,000 thresholds).
- Under s.194C, tax must be deducted **at the time of credit to the payee's account or at the time of payment, whichever is earlier**.
- Since the amount was credited to Devansh Mehta's account on **20 March 2026**, before actual payment on 10 April 2026, the liability to deduct tax (and the deemed date of deduction) arises on **20 March 2026** — i.e., in FY 2025-26. Orchid Biotech Ltd must deduct TDS accordingly, deposit it, and report it in that quarter's TDS return (Form 26Q).

question: Sunrise Beverages Pvt Ltd paid the month's salary to Imran Qureshi on 31 October 2026. Under which Act and section is TDS on this salary governed?
gold: Income-tax Act 2025, s.392(1) - the salary was paid on 31 October 2026, on or after 1 April 2026, so TDS attaches under the new Act (CBDT FAQ Q6.22).
raw_response:
TDS on salary paid to Imran Qureshi is governed by **Section 192 of the Income-tax Act, 1961**.

Employers must deduct tax at source from salary at the time of payment, computed at the average rate of income tax applicable to the employee's estimated annual income.

question: Rathi Cement Works Ltd, a seller, debited TCS in its books on 10 October 2026, and the buyer paid on 25 October 2026. Under which Act is the TCS governed?
gold: Income-tax Act 2025, s.394 - TCS is triggered by the earlier of debit or receipt; the trigger on 10 October 2026 falls on or after 1 April 2026 (CBDT FAQ Q6.21).
raw_response: TCS is governed by the **Income-tax Act, 1961**, specifically **Section 206C** (which requires the seller to collect tax at source from the buyer and deposit it with the government).

question: Trident Software Solutions Ltd, a seller, debited TCS in its books on 2 April 2026, and the buyer paid on 20 April 2026. Under which Act is the TCS governed?
gold: Income-tax Act 2025, s.394 - TCS is triggered by the earlier of debit or receipt; the trigger on 2 April 2026 falls on or after 1 April 2026 (CBDT FAQ Q6.21).
raw_response:
TCS (Tax Collected at Source) by Trident Software Solutions Ltd is governed by the **Income-tax Act, 1961**, specifically **Chapter XVII-BB (Sections 206C to 206CJA)**, which provides for tax collected at source.

Since the seller debited TCS to the buyer's account on **2 April 2026**, it was required to collect the tax from the buyer at that time (Section 206C(1) – collection at debit of buyer's account or receipt, whichever is earlier). The collection having occurred on 2 April 2026, the TCS pertains to AY 2026-27, and payment to the government was due by **7 May 2026** (Section 206C(3)) — hence the 20 April 2026 payment was within time.

(Note: it is *not* governed by the GST Acts, as TCS under GST under Section 52 of CGST Act applies only to e-commerce operators, which is not indicated here.)

question: Migration mapping: section 192 of the 1961 Act (salary - government employees (other than union government)) corresponds to which payment code and section under the Income-tax Act 2025?
raw_response:
**Section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025**, retaining **payment code 192** (salary).

Under the 2025 Act, tax deducted at source on salary is dealt with by section 393, which replaces section 192 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and the payment code assigned to salary in the corresponding Schedule remains 192.

question: Wavelength Telecom LLP is drafting its TDS SOP for salary - government employees (other than union government) to a salary employee. Which provision of the Income-tax Act 2025 tabulates this deduction?
raw_response:
**Section 155 of the Income-tax Act, 2025** (Salaries).

Under Section 155(1), any person responsible for paying income chargeable under the head "Salaries" — including a government (other than the Union/Government of India, i.e., State Government or local authority employees) — must deduct tax at the time of payment, based on the employee's estimated average rate of income tax. This corresponds to Section 192 of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

Note: For Union Government employees, salary TDS payments are routed to the Central Government by any employer, but the deducting provision remains Section 155.

question: (Salary - Government employees (other than Union Government)) Zenith Pumps Pvt Ltd makes a payment of Rs 180,000 to Sanjay Patil on 12 May 2026 during tax year 2026-27. Draft the compliance answer under the Income-tax Act 2025: (i) the payment code for the TDS challan; (ii) the section of the Income-tax Act 2025 governing the TDS; (iii) the rate of TDS; (iv) the date by which the tax so deducted must be deposited.
gold: (i) Payment code 1001; (ii) s.392(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025; (iii) Slab rates (regime-dependent); (iv) deposit by 7 June 2026 (7th of the month following deduction).
raw_response:
**TDS compliance answer – Salary paid to Sanjay Patil (Rs 180,000 on 12 May 2026, PY 2026-27):**

**(i) Payment code for TDS challan:** Payment code **92** (Salary) — to be quoted in Challan ITNS-281 while depositing TDS under section 62 of the Income-tax Act 2025.

**(ii) Governing section:** **Section 62** of the Income-tax Act, 2025 — TDS on income chargeable under the head "Salaries" (the obligation of any responsible person paying salary, including employers such as Zenith Pumps Pvt Ltd).

**(iii) Rate of TDS:** Tax must be deducted at the **average rate of income-tax** computed on the basis of the **normal slab rates** applicable to the employee for the relevant assessment year (estimated salary income for the year, net of permissible deductions such as Chapter VIII deductions, and considering employee-declared investments).

**(iv) Due date for deposit:** Tax deducted on 12 May 2026 must be deposited **by 7 June 2026** (i.e., on or before 7 days from the end of the month in which the deduction is made, per section 397 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 — the relaxed 30 April date applies only to deductions made in March).

*Note:* The "Government employee" carve-out does not apply here — Zenith Pumps Pvt Ltd is a private company, so it itself must deduct and deposit the TDS.

question: Wavelength Telecom LLP is preparing its TDS challan for salary - government employees (other than union government) (February 2027). Under the new Income-tax Act 2025 code scheme, which payment code applies?
raw_response:
**Payment code A‑20** (Salary under section 392 – Government employees other than Union Government).

Note: In the 2025 scheme, the salary TDS provision has been renumbered (section 392), but the challan payment-code convention continues: A‑19 for salary to non-government employees, and **A‑20 for salary to government employees (other than Union Government)** — which is the code Wavelength Telecom LLP should use for this challan.

question: While reconciling challans, Himalaya Interiors LLP finds payment code 1001 on a November 2026 challan. Which nature of payment and governing section does this code denote?
gold: Salary - Government employees (other than Union Government) (s. 392(1))
raw_response:
**Payment code 1001 = Advance Tax**, chargeable under the Income-tax Act, 1961 (governed by Sections 207/210, which mandate advance tax payment in instalments).

As background, the 1000 series on a TAN-based challan denotes Income-tax (non-TDS/TCS): 1001 – Advance Tax, 1002 – Self-Assessment Tax (s.140A), 1003 – Regular Assessment Tax, 1004 – Tax on Regular Assessment, 1005 – Tax on Distributed Profit (s.115-O), and 1007 – Tax on Distributed Income (s.115R).

question: (Salary - employees other than Government) Silverline Jewellers Ltd makes a payment of Rs 1,250,000 to Imran Qureshi on 12 June 2026 during tax year 2026-27. Draft the compliance answer under the Income-tax Act 2025: (i) the payment code for the TDS challan; (ii) the section of the Income-tax Act 2025 governing the TDS; (iii) the rate of TDS; (iv) the date by which the tax so deducted must be deposited.
gold: (i) Payment code 1002; (ii) s.392(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025; (iii) Slab rates (regime-dependent); (iv) deposit by 7 July 2026 (7th of the month following deduction).
raw_response:
**(i) Challan payment code:** 92 (TDS on Salaries)

**(ii) Governing section:** Section 161 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 — TDS on salary (payable/creditable to an employee other than a Government employee).

**(iii) Rate of TDS:** At the average rate of income-tax computed on the basis of the rates in force for FY 2026-27 applicable to the employee's estimated total income (i.e., tax on estimated annual income ÷ estimated annual income), applied to the salary payment — not a flat prescribed rate.

**(iv) Due date of deposit:** The tax must be deducted at the time of payment (12 June 2026) and deposited **within 7 days from the end of the month in which the deduction is made**, i.e., by **7 July 2026** (per Section 403 of the Income-tax Act, 2025; for March deductions, by 30 April).

question: Vasudha Agro Farms Ltd's 2020-21 records cite section 192 for salary - employees other than government. State the current payment code and new-Act provision for the same deduction in July 2026.
raw_response:
**Current position (under the Income-tax Act, 1961, for July 2026 compliance):**

- **Section of deduction:** Section 192 – TDS on salaries (employees other than government employees).
- **Payment code:** **Code 92** – "TDS on Salaries" (used in Challan ITNS-281).

**Under the Income-tax Act, 2025 (effective 1 April 2026):**

- The corresponding provision is **Section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025**, which provides for deduction of tax at source from salaries, replacing Section 192 of the 1961 Act.
- The payment/nature-of-deduction code in the new format continues to be **92** for salary TDS.

**In short:** Section 192 (1961 Act) → **Section 393** (2025 Act); payment code **92** remains the same.

question: (Salary - employees other than Government) Pinnacle Brokerage Ltd makes a payment of Rs 180,000 to Ananya Deshpande on 12 May 2026 during tax year 2026-27. Draft the compliance answer under the Income-tax Act 2025: (i) the payment code for the TDS challan; (ii) the section of the Income-tax Act 2025 governing the TDS; (iii) the rate of TDS; (iv) the date by which the tax so deducted must be deposited.
gold: (i) Payment code 1002; (ii) s.392(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025; (iii) Slab rates (regime-dependent); (iv) deposit by 7 June 2026 (7th of the month following deduction).
raw_response:
**(i) Payment code (challan):** TDS on Salary – payment code **192** (minor head for "Income-tax deducted at source from salaries").

**(ii) Governing section:** **Section 63 of the Income-tax Act, 2025** (TDS on salary by an employer from wages/payable to an employee).

**(iii) Rate of TDS:** Not a flat rate – tax must be deducted at the **average rate of income-tax** computed on the basis of the employee's estimated taxable income for the year, i.e., at the rates applicable under the **First Schedule (slab rates)** for AY 2027-28 (taking into account Ananya's declared investment/particulars in Form 71, if furnished).

**(iv) Due date of deposit:** TDS deducted on **12 May 2026** must be deposited **within 7 days from the end of the month of deduction**, i.e., by **7 June 2026** (as per section 397 of the Act / the corresponding time-limit for non-Government deductors).

question: (Salary - employees other than Government) Kriti Electronics Ltd makes a payment of Rs 250,000 to Kavya Iyer on 12 January 2027 during tax year 2026-27. Draft the compliance answer under the Income-tax Act 2025: (i) the payment code for the TDS challan; (ii) the section of the Income-tax Act 2025 governing the TDS; (iii) the rate of TDS; (iv) the date by which the tax so deducted must be deposited.
gold: (i) Payment code 1002; (ii) s.392(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025; (iii) Slab rates (regime-dependent); (iv) deposit by 7 February 2027 (7th of the month following deduction).
raw_response:
**Compliance answer – Salary TDS under the Income-tax Act, 2025 (payment to Kavya Iyer, non-Government employee)**

1. **Payment code for TDS challan:** Payment code **192** (Salary – other than Government employees).

2. **Governing section:** **Section 387(1)** of the Income-tax Act, 2025 – tax to be deducted at source by an employer from income chargeable under the head "Salaries".

3. **Rate of TDS:** Not a flat rate – tax must be deducted at the **average rate of income-tax** computed on the basis of the rates in force for the financial year, i.e., the tax on the employee's estimated annual taxable income divided by that income (with wages annualised, since employment is not the only source for the employee). TDS is required only if the estimated annual salary exceeds the basic exemption limit (Rs 4,00,000 under the new regime default).

4. **Due date for deposit:** The tax deducted on 12 January 2027 must be deposited to the credit of the Central Government **within 7 days from the end of the month in which the deduction is made (Section 397(1))** – i.e., **on or before 7 February 2027**. (If it were deducted in March, the extended due date of 30 April would apply, but that does not apply here.)

question: A legacy TDS ledger prepared under the 1961 Act shows a deduction under old section 192. The same nature of payment (salary - employees other than government) arises again in May 2026. Which payment code and new-Act section now govern it?
raw_response:
**Payment code:** Minor head (challan) code **92** – TDS on salary (this challan code is retained under the new regime).

**Governing section:** **Section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025** (in place of old section 192 of the 1961 Act), which mandates deduction of tax at source on salary income.

So for the May 2026 salary payment to non-government employees, deduct tax under Section 393, IT Act 2025, and deposit it under challan code 92.

question: (Salary - Indian (Union/Central) Government employees) Emerald Exports Pvt Ltd makes a payment of Rs 550,000 to Sanjay Patil on 12 January 2027 during tax year 2026-27. Draft the compliance answer under the Income-tax Act 2025: (i) the payment code for the TDS challan; (ii) the section of the Income-tax Act 2025 governing the TDS; (iii) the rate of TDS; (iv) the date by which the tax so deducted must be deposited.
gold: (i) Payment code 1003; (ii) s.392(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025; (iii) Slab rates (regime-dependent); (iv) deposit by 7 February 2027 (7th of the month following deduction).
raw_response:
**(i) Payment code for TDS challan:** 192 (Tax Deducted at Source – Salary).

**(ii) Governing section:** Section 392 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (TDS on salary by an employer, i.e., a person paying income chargeable under the head "Salaries").

**(iii) Rate of TDS:** At the average rate of income tax computed on the basis of the employee's estimated income for the financial year (i.e., slab rates applicable to the employee — average of the basic exemption limit and rates on the estimated annual salary). No flat/surcharge-based rate applies; TDS = estimated tax for the year ÷ estimated salary.

**(iv) Due date of deposit:** Tax deducted on 12 January 2027 (month of January 2027) must be deposited within 7 days from the end of the month in which the deduction is made — i.e., **by 7 February 2027**.

question: A CA firm's old template says 'TDS u/s 192' for salary - indian (union/central) government employees. What payment code and section replace this reference for tax year 2026-27?
raw_response:
**No replacement is needed — the template is still correct.**

- **Section:** Section **192** remains the correct provision for TDS on salary. For government employees specifically, the reference can be refined to **Section 192(1A)**, which deals with tax deducted by government employers and paid to Central Government *without* furnishing a challan (via book adjustment / ttable entry). Non-government employers fall under Section 192(1).

- **Payment code:** On **Challan ITNS-281**, the payment code for TDS on salary deducted by the Government is **Code 801 – "TDS Payable by Government"** (as opposed to Code 800 – "TDS Payable by Taxpayer," used by non-government deductors).

So for FY 2026-27, the updated wording should be: **"TDS u/s 192(1A) – salary paid by Central/Union Government employees, paid to credit of Central Government without challan (payment code 801, Challan ITNS-281 / book entry)."**

One note: if the "code" you meant is the nature-of-payment code in **Form 24Q** TDS return, salary under Section 192 continues to be reported as deduction code **192** in Annexure-II — that also hasn't changed.

question: (Salary - Indian (Union/Central) Government employees) Vasudha Agro Farms Ltd makes a payment of Rs 320,000 to Priya Nair on 12 October 2026 during tax year 2026-27. Draft the compliance answer under the Income-tax Act 2025: (i) the payment code for the TDS challan; (ii) the section of the Income-tax Act 2025 governing the TDS; (iii) the rate of TDS; (iv) the date by which the tax so deducted must be deposited.
gold: (i) Payment code 1003; (ii) s.392(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025; (iii) Slab rates (regime-dependent); (iv) deposit by 7 November 2026 (7th of the month following deduction).
raw_response:
**(i) Payment (minor head) code:** 192 (TDS on salaries)

**(ii) Governing section:** Section 195 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (TDS on income chargeable under the head "Salaries"; salary paid by an Indian/Union/Central Government employer falls under this).

**(iii) Rate of TDS:** At the average rate of income tax computed on the basis of Priya Nair's estimated total income for FY 2026-27 under the applicable slab rates (i.e., tax on estimated income ÷ estimated income), not a flat rate — here TDS on Rs 3,20,000 would be computed per the slab applicable to her estimated income for the year.

**(iv) Due date for deposit:** 7 November 2026 — tax deducted on 12 October 2026 must be deposited by 7 November 2026 (7th day of the following month; no government-employer special extended date under the 2025 Act, so the normal 7th-day rule applies).

question: Classify salary - indian (union/central) government employees under the new Act: which section and table governs it for a salary employee?
raw_response:
Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, salary income is governed by **Section 15** (head "Salaries"), read with **Table 3 of Section 15**.

- **Section 15(1)** provides that salaries paid to an employee in the previous year (including salary due and salary in advance) are chargeable as income from salaries.
- **Table 3 to Section 15** specifies the amounts included in "salary" — e.g., dearness allowance, commission, allowances, gratuity, perquisites, advance salary, leave salary, contributions to provident fund, etc.
- **Section 16** then governs the deductions from salary (standard deduction, entertainment allowance, tax on employment).

Salaries of Central/Union and State Government employees fall under the same head — there is no separate section for government employees. Their salary is computed under Section 15 read with Table 3, like any other salaried taxpayer.

question: Below what threshold is TDS not attracted on premature epf withdrawal / accumulated balance due to an employee under the Income-tax Act 2025 (payment code 1004)?
raw_response:
TDS on premature EPF withdrawal (payment code 1004) is not attracted if the accumulated balance due to the employee is **less than ₹50,000**.

Note: Even above this threshold, no TDS applies if the employee has rendered continuous service of 5 years or more, or the withdrawal is due to ill health, closure of employer's business, or other prescribed reasons.

question: Quantify the TDS: payment of Rs 650,000 for premature epf withdrawal / accumulated balance due to an employee by Vindhya Logistics Pvt Ltd in October 2026, tax year 2026-27.
raw_response:
**TDS under Section 192A** (EPF premature withdrawal, service < 5 years):

- Threshold: ₹50,000 — exceeded (₹6,50,000), so TDS applies.
- **If PAN is furnished: 10% × ₹6,50,000 = ₹65,000**
- If PAN not furnished: 20% × ₹6,50,000 = ₹1,30,000 (per amended Sec. 206AA, rate revised from ~34.5% MMR to 20% w.e.f. 1 Oct 2024)

Assuming the employee has furnished PAN, **TDS = ₹65,000**, to be deducted at the time of payment (October 2026) and deposited by 7 November 2026 (30 April 2027 if deducted in March). No TDS applies if service is ≥ 5 years or withdrawal is on account of ill-health, employer closure, etc. (Form 15G/15H can also be furnished to avoid TDS).

question: A legacy TDS ledger prepared under the 1961 Act shows a deduction under old section 192. The same nature of payment (salary - indian (union/central) government employees) arises again in January 2027. Which payment code and new-Act section now govern it?
raw_response:
**Payment code:** 92B – Salary paid by Government (Union/Central Government employees), other than payments to non-residents.

**Governing provision:** Section 394 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (the new Act's renumbered equivalent of old section 192), which requires the Government employer to deduct tax at the average rate of income tax from salary at the time of payment.

So the January 2027 payment of salary to Central/Union Government employees should be reported under payment code **92B**, with tax deducted under **section 394, Income-tax Act, 2025**.

question: Blue Orchid Hospitality LLP makes a payment for premature epf withdrawal / accumulated balance due to an employee to Priya Nair in October 2026, but the payee has not furnished a PAN. At what rate must tax be deducted at source?
raw_response:
**20%.**

Under Section 192A, EPF withdrawal without 5 years of continuous service attracts TDS at 10%. However, since Priya Nair has not furnished her PAN, Section 206AA applies, requiring deduction of tax at the higher of 20% or the normal rate — here, **20%**.

question: A February 2027 payment by Helios Pharma Ltd for premature epf withdrawal / accumulated balance due to an employee to Kavya Iyer requires a challan under the Income-tax Act 2025. State the payment code for this nature of payment.
raw_response:
**Payment code 94** – Payments of accumulated balance of provident fund (TDS deducted under section 192A on premature EPF withdrawal).

So Helios Pharma Ltd must deposit the tax deducted (10% where PAN is furnished and withdrawal is before 5 years of continuous service) via challan ITNS-281 quoting payment code **94** in the TDS payment code column.

question: Tanvi Bhatt receives Rs 650,000 from Pinnacle Brokerage Ltd for premature epf withdrawal / accumulated balance due to an employee in August 2026. What TDS amount should be deducted, assuming full applicability?
raw_response:
**TDS = Rs 65,000 (i.e., 10% of Rs 650,000)**

**Reasoning:**
- EPF withdrawals before 5 years of continuous service are taxable (Sec 10(12) inapplicable), so TDS under **Sec 192A** applies since the withdrawal exceeds **Rs 50,000**.
- Rate: **10%**, provided PAN is furnished by the employee.
- If **PAN is not furnished**, TDS under Sec 206AA applies at the higher of the two — effectively **20% plus cess (20.8%) = Rs 135,200**.

So, assuming PAN is available and the 5-year service condition is not met (full applicability of Sec 192A), Tanvi would receive **Rs 585,000** and **Rs 65,000** would be deducted as TDS.

question: Compute the tax to be deducted at source: Zenith Pumps Pvt Ltd makes a premature epf withdrawal / accumulated balance due to an employee payment of Rs 1,250,000 to Priya Nair in June 2026.
raw_response:
## TDS on Premature EPF Withdrawal

**Applicable Provision:** Section 192A of the Income Tax Act, 1961

**Conditions checked:**
- Withdrawal of ₹12,50,000 — exceeds the ₹50,000 threshold, so TDS applies
- Withdrawal is premature (before 5 years of continuous service), so the withdrawal is **taxable** (had service been ≥ 5 years, it would be exempt and no TDS applies)

**TDS Rate:**
- **10%** where PAN is furnished
- **Maximum Marginal Rate (~34.608%** incl. cess) where PAN is not furnished

**Computation (assuming PAN is provided):**

| Particulars | Amount |
|---|---|
| Accumulated EPF balance paid | ₹12,50,000 |

question: A CA firm's old template says 'TDS u/s 192A' for premature epf withdrawal / accumulated balance due to an employee. What payment code and section replace this reference for tax year 2026-27?

question: Old section 192A applied to premature epf withdrawal / accumulated balance due to an employee under the 1961 Act. From 1 April 2026, which payment code and section of the Income-tax Act 2025 cover this deduction?
raw_response:
## EPF Premature Withdrawal — TDS under the Income-tax Act, 2025

Under the Income-tax Act, 2025 (effective 1 April 2026), the deduction of tax at source on accumulated balances due to an employee from a recognised provident fund (i.e., premature EPF withdrawal not covered by section 80CCB exemption/transfer conditions) is covered by:

- **Section: Section 396** of the Income-tax Act, 2025 — "Payments to employees other than salary" (the equivalent of old section 192A).
- **Payment code:** The prescribed payment code in the statement of TDS for such payment (as notified under the 2025 Act's TDS framework) is the code corresponding to "accumulated balance due to an employee of a provident fund to which the Provident Funds Act, 1925 applies" — commonly reflected as **payment code 94** in reporting (against code 92/94 nomenclature used in the old Form 26Q regime).

**Note:** The substantive charge remains at the same rate — TDS at 10% on the taxable accumulated balance where the withdrawal is not exempt (service < 5 years), with no deduction if the amount is ₹50,000 or less, or if the employee furnishes PAN and the rate would be nil.

*(Practitioners should verify the exact notified payment code from CBDT rules under the 2025 Act, as the codes are being re-notified under section 397/TDS statement rules.)*

question: Migration mapping: section 192A of the 1961 Act (premature epf withdrawal / accumulated balance due to an employee) corresponds to which payment code and section under the Income-tax Act 2025?

question: Prakash Auto Components Ltd's ERP needs the TDS rate for commission or brokerage - insurance configured for tax year 2026-27. What rate applies?

Note: 10% is also the standard rate for non-insurance commission to resident payees, while payments to non-residents under 194D attract 10% (plus cess).

question: Under the Income-tax Act 2025, commission or brokerage - insurance to a resident payee falls under which table/section of the TDS framework?
raw_response: Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, TDS on commission or brokerage paid by an insurance company to a **resident** payee is covered by **Section 391** (which corresponds to Section 194D of the Income-tax Act, 1961). TDS applies at **2%** (or 10% if no PAN is furnished), when the aggregate payment exceeds **₹20,000** in a financial year (threshold effective from 1 April 2025; earlier ₹15,000).

question: Old section 194D applied to commission or brokerage - insurance under the 1961 Act. From 1 April 2026, which payment code and section of the Income-tax Act 2025 cover this deduction?
raw_response:
**Section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025** (effective 1 April 2026) covers tax deduction on commission or brokerage payments, including insurance commission that was earlier dealt with separately under section 194D of the 1961 Act.

The 2025 Act has consolidated the fragmented TDS provisions of the 1961 Act — section 393 merges the old sections 194D (insurance commission) and 194H (commission/brokerage) into a single provision. The deduction applies at the prescribed rate (2%) once aggregate payments to a resident exceed the specified threshold (₹20,000), with the corresponding TDS payment code cited as **393** in the challan/TDS return for such commission and brokerage payments (including insurance commission).

question: The s.393 tables reorganise TDS by payee category. Where does commission or brokerage - insurance to a resident payee belong under the Income-tax Act 2025?
raw_response:
**Commission or brokerage on insurance paid to a resident** falls under the **"commission or brokerage" entry of section 393(1)** of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (which consolidates the old TDS provisions, including erstwhile section 194D of the 1961 Act covering insurance commission).

Key points:

- **Payee category:** Resident (individual/HUF/other resident person).
- **Rate:** 2% of the income (rate as reduced w.e.f. 1 Oct 2024, carried into the 2025 Act).
- **Threshold:** TDS applies only if aggregate commission/brokerage exceeds the prescribed annual limit (₹20,000 in the earlier regime, subject to the 2025 Act's threshold structure).

So it is **not** treated under a separate "insurance commission" head — in the reorganised s.393 table, it is simply commission or brokerage paid to a resident, taxable by deduction at source at 2%.

question: For commission or brokerage - insurance made in December 2026, Sterling Constructions Ltd must quote a nature-of-payment code on its TDS challan under the Income-tax Act 2025. What is the code?

question: Sagar Fisheries Ltd pays Rs 900,000 to Ritu Chauhan in August 2026 for commission or brokerage - others. Compute the TDS amount deductible under the Income-tax Act 2025 (assume the payment is fully subject to TDS).

question: Prakash Auto Components Ltd is drafting its TDS SOP for rent by individual/huf not liable to tax audit to a resident payee. Which provision of the Income-tax Act 2025 tabulates this deduction?

Key points for the SOP:

question: Trident Software Solutions Ltd makes a payment for rent by individual/huf not liable to tax audit to Vikram Malhotra in August 2026, but the payee has not furnished a PAN. At what rate must tax be deducted at source?

question: The payee's PAN is not available for a rent by individual/huf not liable to tax audit payment made by Vasudha Agro Farms Ltd in March 2027. What rate applies under the Income-tax Act 2025?

- The rates in force.

For rent, this works out to **20%**.

question: Zenith Pumps Pvt Ltd pays Rs 90,000 to Sanjay Patil in a single August 2026 payment for rent - plant, machinery or equipment. Is tax deductible at source under the Income-tax Act 2025?

raw_response:
**Yes, TDS applies.**

Under the Income-tax Act, 2025 (which governs FY 2026–27, i.e., from 1 April 2026), TDS on rent for plant, machinery or equipment is covered by **section 193** (TDS on rent).

**Analysis:**
- Zenith Pumps Pvt Ltd is a **company**, so it is liable to deduct TDS on rent regardless of tax audit status (the exemption for individuals/HUFs not covered by audit does not apply).
- The threshold limit is **Rs 50,000 per month or part of a month**. The August 2026 payment of Rs 90,000 exceeds this threshold.
- **Rate:** 2% of the rent (for plant, machinery and equipment), assuming a valid PAN (20% under section 206AB/section 195 if PAN is invalid or not furnished).

**Conclusion:** The company must deduct tax at source of Rs 1,800 (2% of Rs 90,000) and deposit it within the prescribed time (on or before 7 days from the end of the month in which the tax was deducted).

1. **Applicable provision:** Section 193(2) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (corresponding to s.194-IB of the 1961 Act) – TDS on rent by certain individuals/HUFs.
2. **Trigger:** Monthly rent exceeds ₹50,000 (here ₹6,50,000 in aggregate for 2026-27 qualifies).
3. **Rate of TDS:** **2%** of the rent (reduced rate applicable from 1 Oct 2024).
4. **Time of deduction:** Under this provision the tenant is not required to deduct TDS each month; it is deducted at the time of credit of the last rent of the year / when possession is given.
5. **Deposit deadline:** Within **30 days** of deduction (i.e., by 30 May 2027 if deducted on the last credit of FY 2026-27), along with filing Form 26QC (challan-cum-statement). No TAN is required – PAN of the landlord is used.
6. **Challan payment code:** **Code 195 – Rent under section 193(2) [Rent (194-IB)]**.

question: Quantify the TDS: payment of Rs 480,000 for rent - plant, machinery or equipment by Kaveri Textiles Ltd in August 2026, tax year 2026-27.

question: A CA firm's old template says 'TDS u/s 194I(a)' for rent - plant, machinery or equipment. What payment code and section replace this reference for tax year 2026-27?
raw_response:

So the template's *section reference* remains valid; only ensure the deductor selects payment code **94C** and applies the current threshold (₹50,000 per month / ₹6,00,000 p.a. under the 194-I proviso as amended) and the applicable TDS rate (2% for plant & machinery from 01.10.2024; 10% for other assets).

If your old template instead bundles *all* rent (including building) under 194-I(a), that must be corrected — land/building rent must be tagged to **194-I(b), code 94D**.

question: Section 393(7) of the Income-tax Act 2025 deals with higher deduction where PAN is not furnished. For rent - land, building, furniture or fittings by Ganga Steel Traders in July 2026 to a payee without PAN, what rate applies?

Under Section 393(7) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (which corresponds to Section 206AA of the 1961 Act), where the payee fails to furnish PAN, tax is deductible at twice the prescribed rate **or 20%, whichever is higher** — except for payments under the rent provisions (corresponding to Section 194-I), where a flat rate of **20%** applies.

So Ganga Steel Traders must deduct TDS on rent for land, building, furniture or fittings at **20%** of the rent, since the payee has not furnished PAN.

question: A June 2026 payment by Kriti Electronics Ltd for rent - land, building, furniture or fittings to Kavya Iyer requires a challan under the Income-tax Act 2025. State the payment code for this nature of payment.

question: Under the Income-tax Act 2025, Nimbus Media Pvt Ltd makes a payment for transfer of immovable property (other than agricultural land) - consideration to Kavya Iyer (an LLP) in October 2026. Which payment code must be quoted on the TDS challan?

question: The e-filing portal rejects Nova Diagnostics Pvt Ltd's challan for transfer of immovable property (other than agricultural land) - consideration because the nature-of-payment code is missing. Which code should be entered under the Income-tax Act 2025?

question: While configuring its new-Act compliance software for transfer of immovable property (other than agricultural land) - consideration, Annapurna Foods Pvt Ltd needs the nature-of-payment code effective from 1 April 2026. Which code applies?

question: The new Act consolidates TDS into tabular sections. In which table of s.393 (or which section, for TCS) does transfer of immovable property (other than agricultural land) - consideration to a resident payee sit?

**TCS on transfer of certain goods / motor vehicles etc. is separate:** TCS on sale of motor vehicles, luxury goods, and on sale of goods (formerly 206C(1F)/(1H)) is not in s.393 but in **section 394 (TCS)** of the 2025 Act — the corresponding provision for collection of tax at source on sale of goods including immovable-property-type transactions sits in **s.394(1), Table**.

raw_response:

Under this provision, when a business trust (an "investment trust") pays or credits to a **resident** unit holder income by way of **dividend** from a special purpose vehicle, tax is deducted at source at the rate specified in the **Table in section 393(2)**.

(For context, the parallel provisions are: s.393(1) — rent to resident unit holders; s.393(3) — interest to non-residents; s.393(4) — dividend to non-residents — each with its own Table.)

question: Kriti Electronics Ltd is drafting its TDS SOP for business trust distribution - dividend (resident unit holder) to a resident payee. Which provision of the Income-tax Act 2025 tabulates this deduction?

This is the provision that should be cited in Kriti Electronics Ltd's TDS SOP for the distribution (dividend component) to a resident payee.

question: The new Act consolidates TDS into tabular sections. In which table of s.393 (or which section, for TCS) does business trust distribution - dividend (resident unit holder) to a resident payee sit?
raw_response:
This is a **TDS** item, not TCS — so it sits in **section 393** of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (the section replacing the separate 194-series TDS provisions), not in section 394 (which consolidates TCS, the erstwhile 206C provisions).

Specifically, the dividend component of a distribution by a business trust (securitisation trust / InvIT / REIT under the erstwhile s.194LBA(1), i.e., dividend income passed through to the unit holder) to a **resident unit holder** falls in the **Table in clause (1) of section 393** — the table dealing with TDS on payments/incomes to residents — as the entry covering income by way of dividend distributed by a business trust to its unit holders.

Note: the new Act's s.393 tables split by payee type — resident payments generally in the clause (1) table — and TCS collections by business trusts on cash consideration from unit holders would instead fall under s.394 (erstwhile 206CCA). A distribution of dividend income to a resident unit holder is squarely the TDS entry in s.393(1)'s table.

question: Rate of TDS on business trust distribution - rental (reit, resident unit holder) under the Income-tax Act 2025 (payment code 1016)?

question: A CA firm's old template says 'TDS u/s 194LBA' for business trust distribution - dividend (resident unit holder). What payment code and section replace this reference for tax year 2026-27?

For a distribution to a **resident unit holder** in the nature of **dividend** income:

- **Section:** 19A(1)
- **TDS payment (challan) code:** **94G**

(For reference, the parallel new codes under 19A are 94F – interest, resident; 94G – dividend, resident; 94H – interest, non-resident; 94I – dividend, non-resident.)

question: For business trust distribution - rental (reit, resident unit holder) made in September 2026, Prakash Auto Components Ltd must quote a nature-of-payment code on its TDS challan under the Income-tax Act 2025. What is the code?

question: Rathi Cement Works Ltd pays Rs 650,000 to Ritu Chauhan in January 2027 for business trust distribution - rental (reit, resident unit holder). Compute the TDS amount deductible under the Income-tax Act 2025 (assume the payment is fully subject to TDS).

question: Under the Income-tax Act 2025, Meridian Infotech Pvt Ltd makes a payment for business trust distribution - rental (reit, resident unit holder) to Kavya Iyer (a non-resident individual) in November 2026. Which payment code must be quoted on the TDS challan?

question: Meridian Infotech Pvt Ltd makes a payment for business trust distribution - rental (reit, resident unit holder) to Ritu Chauhan in February 2027, but the payee has not furnished a PAN. At what rate must tax be deducted at source?

Under Section 206AA of the Income Tax Act, when a payee fails to furnish their PAN, TDS is deducted at the higher of the prescribed rate or 20%. Since Section 194LBA prescribes a 10% rate for distributions by a business trust to a resident unit holder, the absence of a PAN means tax must be deducted at **20%**.

question: Section 393(7) of the Income-tax Act 2025 deals with higher deduction where PAN is not furnished. For business trust distribution - rental (reit, resident unit holder) by Sterling Constructions Ltd in October 2026 to a payee without PAN, what rate applies?

For a business trust (REIT) distribution of the rental income component to a resident unit holder, the normal rate is 10%, so the higher rate of **20%** applies in the absence of PAN.

question: What is the TDS threshold for interest on securities under the Income-tax Act 2025?
raw_response:
**TDS on interest on securities (Section 393, Income-tax Act, 2025):**

- **Threshold: ₹10,000 per financial year** — tax must be deducted at source only if the aggregate interest on securities paid or payable to a payee during the financial year exceeds ₹10,000.
- **Rate:** 10% of the interest.
- **Key change from the 1961 Act:** Under Section 193 of the old Act, companies/borrowers other than individuals/HUF had *no* threshold (TDS applied to every rupee). The 2025 Act introduces a uniform ₹10,000 threshold for all payers, and removes the earlier condition linking individual/HUF liability to auditable turnover limits.
- TDS is deducted at the time of credit of interest to the payee's account or payment, whichever is earlier.
- Exemptions still apply for interest payable to residents on certain listed dematerialised securities (with the relevant declarations under section 397).

question: Under the Income-tax Act 2025, Corbett Resorts LLP makes a payment for interest on securities to Tanvi Bhatt (a non-resident individual) in May 2026. Which payment code must be quoted on the TDS challan?

Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, the erstwhile separate provision for tax deduction on "interest on securities" (old section 193) has been done away with, and interest (including interest on securities) paid to a non-resident is covered by **section 195** of the Act (TDS on payments/credit to non-residents).

So Corbett Resorts LLP must deduct tax under **section 195** of the Income-tax Act, 2025 and quote the challan payment code applicable to **section 195** (minor head **407** on Form ITNS-281) when depositing the TDS in May 2026.

question: Meridian Infotech Pvt Ltd pays Rs 18,000 to Ananya Deshpande in a single August 2026 payment for interest on securities. Is tax deductible at source under the Income-tax Act 2025?

raw_response:
**Yes, TDS applies.**

Under the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 393, which covers tax deduction on interest, including interest on securities), interest paid to a resident is subject to TDS where it exceeds the prescribed threshold (Rs 10,000).

- Amount paid: **Rs 18,000** – exceeds the threshold
- Meridian Infotech must therefore deduct tax at source at **10%**, i.e. **Rs 1,800**, before making the payment, and deposit it with the government within the prescribed time, furnishing Ananya's PAN.

Note: If Ananya had furnished Form 15G/15H (declaring her income below taxable limits), no deduction would be required.

question: Annapurna Foods Pvt Ltd pays Rs 60,000 to Fatima Sheikh in a single September 2026 payment for interest other than securities - senior citizen payee (bank/po). Is tax deductible at source under the Income-tax Act 2025?

raw_response:
**Yes, tax is deductible at source.**

Under the TDS provision for "interest other than securities" (corresponding to Section 193 of the Income-tax Act, 1961), no deduction is required only if the interest paid to a **resident senior citizen (aged 60 or above)** does **not exceed Rs 50,000** during the financial year.

**Facts:**
- Payee: Fatima Sheikh — senior citizen
- Nature of payment: Interest (other than securities), from a bank
- Amount paid: Rs 60,000 (in a single payment in September 2026)

**Analysis:**
- Rs 60,000 exceeds the Rs 50,000 threshold applicable to senior citizens.
- Therefore, TDS applies at **10%** under Section 193 → **Rs 6,000** must be deducted at source.

**Note:** The deduction is triggered by aggregate interest exceeding the threshold; the fact that it was paid in a single payment does not change the outcome, and TDS applies at the time of credit or payment, whichever is earlier.

question: Under the Income-tax Act 2025, Nimbus Media Pvt Ltd makes a payment for interest other than securities - senior citizen payee (bank/po) to Rakesh Yadav (a foreign company) in October 2026. Which payment code must be quoted on the TDS challan?

question: At what rate is tax deducted at source on interest other than securities - senior citizen payee (bank/po) under the Income-tax Act 2025, given a February 2027 payment of Rs 5,400,000 by Zenith Pumps Pvt Ltd?

question: An auditor asks what payment code 1021 on a tax-year-2026-27 challan signifies. Answer with the nature of payment and the governing section of the Income-tax Act 2025.

question: The s.393 tables reorganise TDS by payee category. Where does interest other than securities - other than senior citizen (bank/po deductor) to a resident payee belong under the Income-tax Act 2025?

Under the 2025 Act's renumbered TDS scheme (set out in the s.393 correspondence tables), the old provisions shift by roughly one section: interest on securities is s.193, dividends s.194, and interest other than securities s.195. So interest paid by a bank or post office to a resident individual (non-senior citizen, within the monetary thresholds and, for banks, subject to the s.195(3) 15G/15H exemption regime) falls under **s.195**.

question: Prakash Auto Components Ltd pays Rs 3,500,000 to Harpreet Gill in June 2026 for interest other than securities - deductor other than bank/post office. Compute the TDS amount deductible under the Income-tax Act 2025 (assume the payment is fully subject to TDS).
raw_response:
**TDS under Section 195 of the Income-tax Act 2025 (corresponding to Section 194A of the 1961 Act) – interest other than securities**

- **Rate:** 10%
- **Threshold:** Rs 5,000 (Rs 50,000 for senior citizens) — here the payment of Rs 35,00,000 far exceeds the threshold.
- **Computation:** Rs 35,00,000 × 10% = **Rs 3,50,000**

Prakash Auto Components Ltd must deduct **Rs 3,50,000** as TDS and deposit it with the government within the prescribed time.

question: The new Act consolidates TDS into tabular sections. In which table of s.393 (or which section, for TCS) does interest other than securities - other than senior citizen (bank/po deductor) to a resident payee sit?
raw_response:
**TDS:** It sits in **Table B of section 397**–style tabular TDS — more precisely, in the **Table to section 397 dealing with interest other than securities (the old s.194A)** of the Income-tax Act, 2025. The tabular TDS section of the 2025 Act splits payees by payment type and residence; the "interest other than securities" table has a specific entry for interest paid to a **resident** (other than the senior-citizen bank/post-office threshold entries), carrying the familiar threshold of ₹5,000 (most payers) / ₹10,000 (banks, co-op societies, post offices) / ₹40,000–₹50,000 (senior citizens), and TDS at 10% under the corresponding slab entry.

**TCS:** TCS is not in the TDS table — it is consolidated separately in **section 397's counterpart, section 397 read with the TCS table in section 397/398 (old s.206C)**, i.e., the collection-at-source table in **section 397** of the 2025 Act.

**Key point:** the resident, non-senior-citizen interest (other than on securities) entry is in the interest-other-than-securities row of the section 393 TDS table, not in the securities (old s.193) row, and TCS sits outside section 393 entirely.

question: A February 2027 payment by Meridian Infotech Pvt Ltd for interest other than securities - deductor other than bank/post office to Devansh Mehta requires a challan under the Income-tax Act 2025. State the payment code for this nature of payment.
raw_response: **Payment code: 94C** — used under Challan ITNS 281 for tax deducted at source on "Interest other than interest on securities" (deductor other than bank/post office), applicable to the payment to Devansh Mehta.

question: Vasudha Agro Farms Ltd asks: up to what limit can interest other than securities - deductor other than bank/post office be paid without TDS under the Income-tax Act 2025?
raw_response:
Under the Income-tax Act, 2025 (section 393, TDS on interest other than interest on securities), where the deductor is **any person other than a bank or post office**, interest (e.g., interest on debentures, loans, deposits other than securities) can be paid **without TDS up to ₹5,000** in aggregate during the financial year. TDS must be deducted once the aggregate interest payable to the payee exceeds this limit.

(For comparison, banks/post offices have a higher threshold of ₹50,000/₹40,000 for certain interest payments.)

question: Old section 194A applied to interest other than securities - deductor other than bank/post office under the 1961 Act. From 1 April 2026, which payment code and section of the Income-tax Act 2025 cover this deduction?
raw_response:
Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, effective 1 April 2026, TDS on interest other than interest on securities (paid by deductors other than banks/post offices) is covered by:

- **Section 393** of the Income-tax Act, 2025
- **Payment code: 194A** (the same code is retained for this nature of payment)

In short, old Section 194A of the 1961 Act maps to **Section 393 read with payment code 194A** under the 2025 Act.

question: (Interest other than securities - deductor other than bank/post office) Wavelength Telecom LLP makes a payment of Rs 3,500,000 to Ananya Deshpande on 12 March 2027 during tax year 2026-27. Draft the compliance answer under the Income-tax Act 2025: (i) the payment code for the TDS challan; (ii) the section of the Income-tax Act 2025 governing the TDS; (iii) the rate of TDS; (iv) the date by which the tax so deducted must be deposited.

**(i) Payment code:** TDS on interest other than securities is challan minor head **800** (other than company deductor, since Wavelength Telecom LLP is not a company); company deductors use code 94.

**(ii) Governing section:** **Section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025** (TDS on interest other than interest on securities) — corresponding to Section 194A of the 1961 Act.

**(iii) Rate of TDS:** **10%** of the interest. Since the payment to Ananya Deshpande exceeds the monetary threshold (Rs 10,000 in a tax year; Rs 50,000 for specified category of payees), TDS applies. No TDS is required if she furnishes Form 15H/15G, as applicable.

**(iv) Due date of deposit:** Tax deducted in **March 2027** must be deposited **on or before 30 April 2027** (tax deducted in March may be deposited by 30 April of the following month; deduction in any other month must be deposited within 7 days from the end of that month).

question: (Interest other than securities - deductor other than bank/post office) Nova Diagnostics Pvt Ltd makes a payment of Rs 250,000 to Nikhil Bansal on 12 November 2026 during tax year 2026-27. | Item | Answer |

question: The new Act consolidates TDS into tabular sections. In which table of s.393 (or which section, for TCS) does interest other than securities - deductor other than bank/post office to a resident payee sit?
raw_response:
Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, TDS provisions are consolidated in the **Table to section 393(1)** (TCS is dealt with separately in **section 394**).

Interest (other than interest on securities) paid to a **resident** by a deductor who is **not a bank or post office** — i.e., the provision formerly in s.194A of the 1961 Act as it applied to non-bank/PO payers — appears in **Part II of the Table to section 393**, at the entry corresponding to the former s.194A (other interest), which prescribes deduction at 10% where aggregate interest exceeds the prescribed threshold (₹5,000, or ₹50,000 for senior citizens in the banking cases).

Note: the bank/post-office scenarios of the old s.194A are carved out as separate entries in the same Table (with the higher ₹50,000 threshold), and interest on "specified securities"/debentures to residents falls under a distinct row reflecting the former s.194A(3)/194A(3A) regime (threshold ₹5,000).

question: A challan for a September 2026 payment quotes payment code 1022. What nature of payment does this code represent under the Income-tax Act 2025?
gold: Interest other than securities - deductor other than bank/post office (s. 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 5(iii)])
raw_response:
**Payment code 1022 represents Tax Collected at Source (TCS).**

Under the Income-tax Act 2025 (mirroring the minor-head convention of ITNS 281 under the earlier 1961 Act):

- **1022 – TCS**: used when a collector (e.g., seller of specified goods, scrap, motor vehicles, overseas tour packages, etc.) deposits tax collected at source from the buyer under the TCS provisions (Chapter XIX-B related provisions).

Note the distinction from related codes:
- **1021** – Tax Deducted at Source (TDS)
- **1020** – Advance tax / Self-assessment categories handled under different challans

So a September 2026 deposit quoting code 1022 is a deposit of tax **collected** at source by the deductor in the capacity of a *collector*, not deducted by them.

question: An auditor asks what payment code 1023 on a tax-year-2026-27 challan signifies. Answer with the nature of payment and the governing section of the Income-tax Act 2025.
gold: Contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee Individual/HUF (s. 393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 6(i).D(a)])
raw_response:
**Payment code 1023 (ITNS 280 minor head): Securities Transaction Tax (STT).**

- **Nature of payment:** Tax collected on taxable securities transactions (purchase/sale of equity shares, units of equity-oriented mutual funds, etc.) on a recognised stock exchange, and on the sale of units of equity-oriented funds to the fund — collected and paid to the government by the recognised stock exchange or the mutual fund, as the case may be.
- **Governing law:** Chapter X of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (which corresponds to Chapter VII of the erstwhile Income-tax Act, 1961), read with the applicable rates notified in the Finance Act.

So the auditor should note that challan code 1023 represents STT deposited under the Income-tax Act, 2025 — not regular advance tax, self-assessment tax, or TDS (which appear under codes 100/305, 300/400, and 106/107 respectively).

question: Classify contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee individual/huf under the new Act: which section and table governs it for a resident payee?
raw_response:
# TDS on Contract / Sub-Contract Payments (Individual/HUF Payee)

**Governing provision:** **Section 194C** of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (i.e., the new Income-tax Act, 2025's corresponding provision on payments to contractors).

**Rate:** **1%** where the payee is an **individual or HUF** (2% for other payees), as per the rates specified in the provision (earlier under Table in Part II of the First Schedule / Section 194C(1)).

## Key points

- **Section 194C** applies to any payment to a **resident** contractor/sub-contractor for carrying out any **work** (including advertising, broadcasting/telecasting, carriage of goods/passengers other than railways).
- **Threshold:** TDS required only if aggregate payment exceeds **₹30,000 in a single contract** or **₹1,00,000 in aggregate during the financial year**.
- Rate of **1% (individual/HUF)** and **2% (others)** — the payee's status determines the rate, not the payer's.
- **Section 194C(4):** No deduction if such income is offered in the payee's books of account under **Section 44AD/44ADA** and PAN/Aadhaar is furnished.
- **Note:** If the payee is a **non-resident**, the payment falls under **Section 195** instead (Section 194C applies only to residents).

**Answer: Section 194C — 1% TDS on contract/sub-contract payments to a resident individual or HUF, subject to the ₹30,000/₹1,00,000 threshold.**

question: (Contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee Individual/HUF) Annapurna Foods Pvt Ltd makes a payment of Rs 250,000 to Priya Nair on 12 May 2026 during tax year 2026-27. Draft the compliance answer under the Income-tax Act 2025: (i) the payment code for the TDS challan; (ii) the section of the Income-tax Act 2025 governing the TDS; (iii) the rate of TDS; (iv) the date by which the tax so deducted must be deposited.
gold: (i) Payment code 1023; (ii) s.393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 6(i).D(a)] of the Income-tax Act 2025; (iii) 1%; (iv) deposit by 7 June 2026 (7th of the month following deduction).
raw_response:
**Compliance Answer – Payment to Priya Nair (Individual/HUF contractor), FY 2026-27**

**(i) Payment code for TDS challan:** Payment code **192** (Code 192 – "Tax deducted at source under section 393 – Contractor, sub-contractor"). *(The corresponding code under the old Act's Annexure-I was 206.)*

**(ii) Governing section:** **Section 393** of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (deduction of tax from payments to contractors and sub-contractors – successor to section 194C of the 1961 Act).

**(iii) Rate of TDS:** **1%** of the gross amount, since the payee is an Individual/HUF (it would be 2% for a payee other than an individual/HUF). The threshold is exceeded (single payment > Rs 30,000), so tax must be deducted on the full Rs 250,000 → **TDS = Rs 2,500**.

**(iv) Due date for deposit:** Tax deducted on **12 May 2026** must be deposited within **7 days from the end of the month of deduction**, i.e., by **7 June 2026**. (Had the deduction fallen in March, the extended due date of 30 April would apply; since Priya Nair is not required to get her accounts audited, no concessional "quarterly" deposit date applies to the deductor.)

question: What is the TDS threshold for contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee individual/huf under the Income-tax Act 2025?
raw_response:
Under the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 393, corresponding to Section 194C of the 1961 Act), tax is deductible on payments to a resident contractor/sub-contractor (individual or HUF) at **1%** of the payment, once the payment exceeds:

- **₹30,000** in a single payment/transaction, **or**
- **₹1,00,000** in aggregate during the financial year.

Key points:
- Deduction applies only when the aggregate exceeds the threshold; if total annual payments stay at or below ₹1,00,000, no TDS even if individual payments exceed ₹30,000.
- No TAN/PAN issues: if the payee furnishes a PAN, 1% applies; if PAN is not furnished, TDS is at the higher rate under the relevant provision (20% or maximum rate).
- No deduction is required where the individual/HUF pays is for personal purposes (not business/profession).

question: Under the Income-tax Act 2025, Meridian Infotech Pvt Ltd makes a payment for contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee individual/huf to Arjun Reddy (an LLP) in February 2027. Which payment code must be quoted on the TDS challan?
raw_response:
**Section/payment code: 194C** (contractor – individual/HUF).

Under Section 194C, payments to contractors/sub-contractors who are individuals or HUFs attract TDS at 1%, and this is the code to be selected while furnishing the TDS challan. (If the payee were a firm/LLP/company, the rate would be 2%, but the challan section code remains 194C.)

Note: an LLP is technically not an individual/HUF — since Arjun Reddy is stated to be an LLP, it would actually fall in the 2% category; however, the challan code remains **194C** in either case, only the rate differs.

question: Zenith Pumps Pvt Ltd makes a payment for contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee other than individual/huf to Meera Joshi in May 2026, but the payee has not furnished a PAN. At what rate must tax be deducted at source?
raw_response:
**Rate: 20%**

Under Section 194C, payments to contractors other than individual/HUF attract TDS at 2%. However, since the payee (Meera Joshi) has not furnished a PAN, Section 206AA applies, overriding the lower contractual rate. Tax must therefore be deducted at **20%** of the payment amount.

question: A CA firm's old template says 'TDS u/s 194C' for contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee individual/huf. What payment code and section replace this reference for tax year 2026-27?
raw_response:
**Short answer: Section 194C does not change by itself — but from 1 April 2026, it maps to Section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (which replaces the 1961 Act for tax year 2026-27).**

Details:

1. **New section reference:** Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, contractor/sub-contractor TDS is covered by **Section 393** (with the threshold of ₹30,000 single / ₹1,00,000 aggregate and rates of 1%/2% retained). So the template note should read "TDS u/s 393" for payments from 01-04-2026 onwards, while "TDS u/s 194C" remains correct for payments up to 31-03-2026.

2. **Payment/nature-of-payment code:** In TDS returns (Form 26Q/4Q), the nature-of-payment code for contractors remains **94C** — the coding scheme continues under the 2025 Act, so the code does not change; only the section reference displayed/selected does.

3. **Practical note:** Update the template to a conditional wording (e.g., "TDS u/s 194C / Sec. 393, IT Act 2025, as applicable to the financial year") since deductions for 2025-26 still cite 194C, and the 2025 Act's provisions take effect only from 01-04-2026, pending final notified rules/returns software reflecting the new section mapping.

question: The payee's PAN is not available for a contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee other than individual/huf payment made by Sterling Constructions Ltd in December 2026. What rate applies under the Income-tax Act 2025?
raw_response:
**20%.**

Under Section 397(1) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, payments to a contractor (other than an individual/HUF) attract TDS at 2% (and at 1% where the payee is an individual/HUF). However, where the deductee fails to furnish their PAN, Section 397(5) mandates that tax be deducted at the higher rate of **20%** (or the applicable rate, if higher) — the counterpart of Section 206AA of the 1961 Act.

So Sterling Constructions Ltd must deduct TDS at **20%** on the sub-contractor payment made in December 2026, since the payee is a non-individual/non-HUF entity whose PAN is unavailable.

question: The e-filing portal rejects Wavelength Telecom LLP's challan for contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee other than individual/huf because the nature-of-payment code is missing. Which code should be entered under the Income-tax Act 2025?
raw_response:
**Code 94C** — "Payments to contractors/sub-contractors, payee other than an individual/HUF."

Under the Income-tax Act, 1961 this corresponded to Section 194C; in the Income-tax Act, 2025 the TDS provision for contractor payments is carried in Section 394, and the e-filing/challan nature-of-payment code remains **94C** for a contractor/sub-contractor payee that is not an individual or HUF (94C is used where TDS applies at the flat rate without the turnover threshold benefit; code 194C-type threshold treatment for individual/HUF payees is the separate code 94C's counterpart — code **94C** vs. **194C(2)** individual/HUF code **94C**).

In short: select **94C (Section 394, Income-tax Act 2025)** in the TDS challan/nature-of-payment field.

question: (Contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee other than Individual/HUF) Rathi Cement Works Ltd makes a payment of Rs 650,000 to Devansh Mehta on 12 January 2027 during tax year 2026-27. Draft the compliance answer under the Income-tax Act 2025: (i) the payment code for the TDS challan; (ii) the section of the Income-tax Act 2025 governing the TDS; (iii) the rate of TDS; (iv) the date by which the tax so deducted must be deposited.

| (i) Payment code (TDS challan) | **94C** (Minor head for TDS on contracts under section 393) |

question: Zenith Pumps Pvt Ltd is preparing its TDS challan for contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee other than individual/huf (February 2027). Under the new Income-tax Act 2025 code scheme, which payment code applies?
raw_response:
Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, TDS on payments to contractors/sub-contractors (the counterpart of section 194C of the 1961 Act) is governed by **section 394 of the Income-tax Act, 2025**.

Accordingly, for a contractor/sub-contractor payment where the payee is a company/firm (i.e., other than an individual or HUF), Zenith Pumps Pvt Ltd must select the TDS challan (ITNS-281) payment code assigned to **section 394 — payee other than individual/HUF** (the analogue of the old 194C "payee other than individual/HUF" code under the 1961 Act scheme, i.e., the company code rather than the "A" code used for individual/HUF payees).

**Practical caveats:**
- TDS @ 1% (other than individual/HUF payee) under section 394, to be deposited by 7 March 2027 (February being a month other than March).
- Verify the exact numeric challan code against the CBDT notification/challan drop-down in effect for FY 2026-27, as the new code list under the 2025 Act is notified separately and updated periodically.

question: (Contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee other than Individual/HUF) Vindhya Logistics Pvt Ltd makes a payment of Rs 900,000 to Joseph Kurien on 12 December 2026 during tax year 2026-27. Draft the compliance answer under the Income-tax Act 2025: (i) the payment code for the TDS challan; (ii) the section of the Income-tax Act 2025 governing the TDS; (iii) the rate of TDS; (iv) the date by which the tax so deducted must be deposited.

**(ii) Governing section:** Section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (corresponding to section 194C of the 1961 Act) — TDS on contracts, where the payee is other than an individual or HUF.

**(iii) Rate of TDS:** 2% of the payment (since payee is not an individual/HUF; 1% applies only to payments to individuals/HUF). Tax deducted = 2% × Rs 9,00,000 = **Rs 18,000**.

**(iv) Due date for deposit:** The tax must be deposited **by 7 January 2027** (i.e., on or before seven days from the end of the month — December 2026 — in which the deduction was made), per the time-of-payment provisions of the Act.

*(Note: Since the payee category is stated as other than individual/HUF, the 2% rate applies notwithstanding that "Joseph Kurien" appears to be an individual — the answer follows the stated payee classification.)*

question: Zenith Pumps Pvt Ltd is drafting its TDS SOP for contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee other than individual/huf to a resident payee. Which provision of the Income-tax Act 2025 tabulates this deduction?
raw_response: **Section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025** (Table/Schedule of TDS provisions) — specifically the entry corresponding to Section 194C of the 1961 Act, covering payments to resident contractors/sub-contractors (excluding individual/HUF payees), i.e., deduction of tax on contract payments at the prescribed rate.

question: Section 393(7) of the Income-tax Act 2025 deals with higher deduction where PAN is not furnished. For payment by individual/huf (contract work, professional fees, commission) not covered by 194c/194h/194j by Nova Diagnostics Pvt Ltd in June 2026 to a payee without PAN, what rate applies?
raw_response:
**20%** applies.

Under Section 393(7) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, where the deductee fails to furnish PAN, tax is deductible at the higher of (a) 20%, or (b) the rate specified in the relevant provision (i.e., Section 194C/194H/194J equivalents, which are generally 1%/2%, 5%, and 10% respectively). Since the payer, Nova Diagnostics Pvt Ltd, is a **company** (not an individual/HUF), it cannot claim the exemption under Section 197A-equivalent provisions available to individuals/HUFs not subject to tax audit — the 20% higher rate therefore applies to all such payments (contract work, professional fees, commission) made to the payee without PAN in June 2026.

question: Silverline Jewellers Ltd is preparing its TDS challan for payment by individual/huf (contract work, professional fees, commission) not covered by 194c/194h/194j (June 2026). Under the new Income-tax Act 2025 code scheme, which payment code applies?
raw_response:
**Section: 194M (new Act: Section 397) — Payment code 4H (minor head 400).**

Where an individual/HUF is liable to deduct tax on contract work, professional fees, or commission (not requiring tax audit / not covered under 194C, 194H, 194J), the deposit is under the composite provision — old Section 194M, carried forward as **Section 397 of the Income-tax Act, 2025**. The TDS challan payment code remains **4H**.

question: (Contractor/sub-contractor payment - payee other than Individual/HUF) Trident Software Solutions Ltd makes a payment of Rs 550,000 to Sanjay Patil on 12 September 2026 during tax year 2026-27. Draft the compliance answer under the Income-tax Act 2025: (i) the payment code for the TDS challan; (ii) the section of the Income-tax Act 2025 governing the TDS; (iii) the rate of TDS; (iv) the date by which the tax so deducted must be deposited.
gold: (i) Payment code 1024; (ii) s.393(1) [Table: Sl. No. 6(i).D(b)] of the Income-tax Act 2025; (iii) 2%; (iv) deposit by 7 October 2026 (7th of the month following deduction).

**Compliance Answer (Contractor payment, payee not being an Individual/HUF)**

- **(i) Challan payment (min) code:** 94C (TDS on payments to contractors/sub-contractors).
- **(ii) Governing section:** Section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (TDS on payments to contractors and sub-contractors).
